items.question: What is the recommended IAS for autorotation following an engine failure?
items.explanation: Autorotation is performed at 75 kt for best glide performance.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-12

items.question: At what altitude should the autorotation flare be initiated?
items.explanation: The flare is initiated at approximately 50 ft AGL.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-13

items.question: In case of engine fire in flight, what is the first action?
items.explanation: First action is to reduce collective to minimize power and fire intensity.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-18

items.question: Which system must be switched OFF during an engine fire procedure?
items.explanation: Engine fire requires fuel shut-off, generator and battery OFF.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-19

items.question: What is the first action in case of smoke or fire of electrical origin?
items.explanation: Battery must be switched OFF first in case of electrical fire.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-22

items.question: If tail rotor control is lost in cruise flight, what is the recommended procedure?
options: Reduce power and adjust speed for controlled flight
items.explanation: Tail rotor control loss in cruise is handled by adjusting power and speed for controlled flight.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-25

items.question: In a hover, if tail rotor thrust is lost, what should the pilot do?
options: Apply forward cyclic to gain speed
items.explanation: Reducing collective fully minimizes torque and allows controlled descent.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-26

items.question: What is the maximum IAS permitted in case of hydraulic failure?
items.explanation: Max speed after hydraulic failure is 100 kt.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-31

items.question: What is the recommended procedure after hydraulic failure?
items.explanation: After hydraulic failure, land as soon as practicable.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-32

items.question: If both fuel pumps fail, what is the maximum altitude permitted?
items.explanation: Both fuel pumps failed limits flight to max 8000 ft.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-36

items.question: “Land as soon as possible” means:
options: Land at nearest site where safe landing can be made
Land only if technical crew is available
items.explanation: It means landing at the nearest site where safe landing can be made.

items.question: “Land as soon as practicable” indicates:
options: Land at nearest airfield with expected assistance
items.explanation: Landing at the nearest airfield with expected assistance is correct.

items.question: During engine failure in cruise with external load, what is the first action?
items.explanation: First apply autorotation procedure, then jettison load.

items.question: In hover with engine failure and sling load, what must be done?
options: Release load, control yaw, forward cyclic, cushion landing
items.explanation: The procedure is to release load and use cyclic/collective for safe landing.

items.question: In hover during engine failure with hoist load, the correct action is:
options: Release load, control yaw, forward cyclic, cushion landing
Perform running landing with load attached
items.explanation: Pilot must jettison load and control yaw with cyclic/collective.

items.question: After hydraulic failure, recommended safety speed range is:
items.explanation: Recommended speed after HYDR warning is 40–60 kt.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-34

items.question: If control load feedback occurs before reaching safety speed after HYDR warning, pilot must:
items.explanation: Cut-off must be set to OFF if feedback is felt before speed is reached.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-35

items.question: In case of display malfunction (blanking), the pilot should:
options: Use standby instruments and visual references
items.explanation: Pilot must use standby instruments and external references.

items.question: First action in case of smoke of electrical origin is:
items.explanation: Electrical fire requires switching off battery first.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-22

items.question: With complete tail rotor thrust loss in hover, action is:
items.explanation: Collective must be reduced fully in hover tail rotor failure.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-26

items.question: In cruise, loss of tail rotor control should be handled by:
items.explanation: Adjust speed/power to maintain controllability.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-25

items.question: If electrical jettison of load fails, what must the pilot use?
items.explanation: Mechanical release is used if electrical jettison fails.

items.question: If load indicator shows incorrect status (LD ON light anomaly), the action is:
items.explanation: Abort sling mission if load indicator fails in hover.

items.question: If fuel pumps fail, maximum altitude permitted is:
items.explanation: Both pumps failed limits altitude to 8000 ft.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-36

items.question: Rotor brake inoperative in flight requires:
items.explanation: Rotor brake inoperative in flight has no operational consequence.

items.question: Bleed valve failure requires pilot to:
items.explanation: Procedure is to land as soon as practicable after bleed valve failure.

items.question: ICS failure during hoist operation means:
options: Complete present hoist or abort depending on circumstances
items.explanation: Depending on conditions, either complete or abort mission.

items.question: Static electricity hazard when using cargo hook means:
options: Ground crew must stay on right side
Ground crew must wear rubber gloves
items.explanation: Ground personnel must wear rubber gloves to avoid static shocks.

items.question: At what speed must float arming not be performed?
items.explanation: Float arming is prohibited above 80 kt.
references: RFM H125 SUP.10 – Emergency Floats – p. 3-10-4

items.question: During autorotation over water with floats, at what height is the flare initiated?
items.explanation: With floats, flare is initiated at approximately 70 ft.
references: RFM H125 SUP.10 – Emergency Floats – p. 3-10-5

items.question: After ditching with floats, what must be done with doors?
items.explanation: After ditching, actuate door jettison handles for evacuation.
references: RFM H125 SUP.10 – Emergency Floats – p. 3-10-6

items.question: If gyro-compass failure occurs, pilot must:
items.explanation: Procedure requires pilot to keep feet on pedals to maintain control.

items.question: In case of major governor failure, EBCAU engages and N1 must be kept above:
items.explanation: EBCAU requires N1 above 80% when below 20,000 ft.

items.question: If N1 still available during EBCAU mode, what is the recommended landing?
items.explanation: Land as soon as practicable if N1 indication remains available in EBCAU.

items.question: Minor FADEC failure requires pilot to:
options: Avoid abrupt power changes, maintain IAS below VNE
items.explanation: Minor FADEC failure procedure: avoid abrupt power changes and remain below VNE.

items.question: First action in engine bay fire during start-up:
options: Fuel pump OFF, CRANK 10 sec, rotor brake ≤170 rpm
items.explanation: Fuel pump off, crank for 10 seconds, rotor brake applied ≤170 rpm.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-18

items.question: If engine fire in flight, first collective action is:
items.explanation: In flight fire, collective must be reduced to minimize power.
references: RFM H125 Section 3 – Emergency Procedures – p. 3-19

items.question: During electrical failure with VEMD screens unreadable, procedure is:
items.explanation: If VEMD is unreadable, apply VEMD screen failure checklist.

items.question: Which recommendation means an immediate landing without delay?
items.explanation: "LAND IMMEDIATELY" is self-explanatory and requires landing without delay.

items.question: Which recommendation means the flight can be continued as planned with repair at the destination?
items.explanation: "CONTINUE FLIGHT" means the flight can be continued as planned and repair carried out at destination according to the maintenance manual.

items.question: On the console, what is the function of the [HORN] switch?
options: To activate the audio warning system
To reset the caution and warning panel
items.explanation: Section 3.1 states that the [HORN] switch is used to activate the audio warning. The pilot at the controls shall wear an adequate headset to monitor audio warnings through the ICS.

items.question: What happens when a red warning appears on the Caution and Warning Panel (CWP)?
items.explanation: Section 3.1 specifies that a gong is generated each time a red warning appears on the CWP.

items.question: A continuous 310 Hz tone is heard when:
items.explanation: The B3e manual states that a continuous 310 Hz tone is heard when rotor speed Nr is below 360 rpm.

items.question: An intermittent 310 Hz tone is heard when:
items.explanation: Section 3.1 states that an intermittent 310 Hz tone is heard when Nr is above 410 rpm.

items.question: A 285 Hz tone is heard when:
items.explanation: Section 3.1 describes a continuous 285 Hz tone when maximum takeoff rating is exceeded, including when transient power limits are exceeded or will be exceeded during a rapid power increase.

items.question: In case of engine flame-out in cruise flight over land, what is the correct sequence of the first three immediate actions?
options: Collective – REDUCE; IAS – set Vy; Twist grip – IDLE
IAS – set Vy; Collective – REDUCE; Twist grip – IDLE
Twist grip – IDLE; IAS – set Vy; Collective – REDUCE
Collective – REDUCE; Twist grip – IDLE; IAS – set Vy
items.explanation: Section 3.2 states that after engine flame-out in cruise, the pilot must first REDUCE collective to maintain NR, then set IAS to Vy, then move the twist grip to IDLE.
references: RFM AS350 Section 3.2 – Engine flame-out – p. 3-1

items.question: During an autorotation landing over land after engine flame-out, which combination of control actions is recommended at approximately 20–25 ft (6–8 m)?
options: Collective – gradually increase; Cyclic – forward to adopt a slightly nose-up attitude (< 10°); Pedals – adjust to cancel sideslip
Collective – reduce fully; Cyclic – full aft; Pedals – centered
Collective – maintain; Cyclic – neutral; Pedals – full right pedal
Collective – increase then immediately reduce to full low pitch; Cyclic – neutral; Pedals – adjust
items.explanation: Section 3.2 specifies that at 20–25 ft the pilot should gradually increase collective to reduce rate of descent and speed, move the cyclic forward to a slightly nose-up attitude (< 10°), and adjust pedals to remove any sideslip.
references: RFM AS350 Section 3.2 – Engine flame-out – p. 3-1

items.question: Immediately after touchdown in an autorotation landing over land, what should the pilot do with collective, cyclic and pedals?
options: Adjust collective, cyclic and pedals to control the ground run
Move cyclic fully aft and collective to full low pitch
Apply rotor brake immediately regardless of NR
Lower collective to idle stop and center cyclic without pedal input
items.explanation: In Section 3.2 the checklist states that after touchdown the pilot must adjust cyclic, collective and pedals to control the ground run before placing collective to full low pitch.
references: RFM AS350 Section 3.2 – Engine flame-out – p. 3-1

items.question: During autorotation over water after engine flame-out, what is the maximum indicated airspeed recommended at ditching?
items.explanation: Section 3.2 states that during autorotation over water the helicopter should ditch with minimum forward speed, IAS less than 30 kt, and minimum rate of descent.
references: RFM AS350 Section 3.2 – Engine flame-out – p. 3-2

items.question: In case of engine flame-out in hover IGE, which sequence of actions is recommended?
options: Collective – MAINTAIN; Pedals – CONTROL YAW; Collective – INCREASE as needed to cushion touchdown
Collective – FULL LOW PITCH; Cyclic – forward; Pedals – neutral
Collective – reduce fully; Twist grip – IDLE; Cyclic – flare
Collective – MAINTAIN; Apply rotor brake; Pedals – centered
items.explanation: The hover IGE subsection of Section 3.2 specifies that after engine flame-out the pilot should maintain collective, control yaw with pedals, then increase collective as needed to cushion the touchdown.
references: RFM AS350 Section 3.2 – Engine flame-out – p. 3-2

items.question: In case of engine flame-out in hover OGE (clear area, outside the HV diagram), what is the first collective action according to the procedure?
items.explanation: For hover OGE outside the HV diagram, Section 3.2 states that the first action is to lower collective to FULL LOW PITCH before using cyclic to gain airspeed and applying the autorotation procedure.
references: RFM AS350 Section 3.2 – Engine flame-out – p. 3-2

items.question: After engine flame-out, what is the correct order of the first three actions in the in-flight relighting procedure?
options: [FUEL P] or [FUEL PUMP] – ON; [GENE] – OFF; Engine starting selector – OFF then ON
[GENE] – OFF; [FUEL P] or [FUEL PUMP] – ON; Engine starting selector – OFF then ON
Engine starting selector – OFF then ON; [FUEL P] or [FUEL PUMP] – ON; [GENE] – OFF
[FUEL P] or [FUEL PUMP] – ON; Engine starting selector – ON; [GENE] – OFF
items.explanation: Section 3.2 (In-flight relighting) specifies that the pilot must first switch the fuel pump ON, then switch the generator OFF, then set the engine starting selector OFF and back to ON to start the automatic relight sequence.
references: RFM AS350 Section 3.2 – Engine flame-out – p. 3-3

items.question: What is the minimum height required to complete the in-flight relighting procedure after an engine flame-out?
items.explanation: At the end of the in-flight relighting procedure, Section 3.2 notes that at least 1000 ft (300 m) are necessary to complete the relight after flame-out.
references: RFM AS350 Section 3.2 – Engine flame-out – p. 3-3

items.question: If the VEMD upper screen fails, what happens on the lower screen?
options: The 3-parameter engine page is automatically displayed
The lower screen also switches off
The FLI symbology is permanently lost
items.explanation: Section 3.5 VEMD Screen Failures states that if the top screen fails, the 3-parameter engine page is automatically displayed on the lower screen.

items.question: If both VEMD screens fail, what governs the maximum authorized power?
options: A level-flight IAS law: 100 kt at 0 Hp, minus 2 kt per 1000 ft
The last recorded FLI value before failure
There is no longer any power limit
items.explanation: Section 3.5 states that with both VEMD screens failed, the maximum authorized power is the power needed for level flight at IAS = 100 kt at 0 Hp, decreasing 2 kt per 1000 ft, landing as soon as practicable with NR constant at 394 rpm.

items.question: In case of NR indication failure, how can rotor speed still be monitored?
options: It cannot be monitored at all
items.explanation: Section 3.5 Abnormal NR/N2 Indications states that with NR indication failure, NR reading is given by the N2 pointer; maintain collective to keep TRQ above 10% and land as soon as practicable.

items.question: In case of N2 indication failure, what system may become unavailable?
items.explanation: Section 3.5 notes that with N2 indication failure, the EBCAU (emergency governor mode) may not be available.

items.question: In case of engine oil temperature over limit, what is the first action?
options: Set airspeed to 80 KIAS and check if temperature decreases
Shut down the engine in flight
items.explanation: Section 3.5 Abnormal Engine Parameter Indications: for oil temperature over limit, set airspeed to 80 KIAS (148 km/h); if temperature decreases, land as soon as practicable, otherwise land as soon as possible.

items.question: In case of confirmed low engine oil pressure (ENG P light test completed and light stays on), what is the procedure?
options: Land immediately, applying the autorotation procedure
Reduce power and land as soon as possible
items.explanation: Section 3.5 Low Engine Oil Pressure: if the ENG P caution is confirmed after a CWP light test, land immediately and apply the autorotation procedure.

items.question: In case of TOT indication failure, what should be done with the heating and demisting system?
items.explanation: Section 3.5 states that with TOT indication failure, the heating and demisting system must be switched off, the engine must not be started on the ground, and the pilot should land as soon as practicable.

items.question: If the generator overvoltage exceeds 31.5 V, what is the correct response?
options: Switch GEN/GENE OFF and land as soon as practicable
items.explanation: Section 3.5 Abnormal Electrical Parameter Indications: for generator overvoltage above 31.5 V, switch GEN (or GENE) OFF, monitor the CWP, apply the GENE procedure, and land as soon as practicable.

items.question: If the generator current red underline is flashing (overcurrent), what should the pilot do?
options: Switch off unnecessary equipment and continue flight
Shut down the generator and land as soon as possible
items.explanation: Section 3.5: a flashing red underline on generator current indicates an overcurrent condition — switch off unnecessary equipment and continue flight.

items.question: What is the procedure for Main Gear Box (MGB) low oil pressure below 1 bar?
options: Reduce power and land as soon as possible
items.explanation: Section 3.6 Transmission Alarms: MGB oil pressure below 1 bar (14.5 psi) requires reducing power and landing as soon as possible; if a safe landing isn't possible, continue to the nearest suitable site at minimum power speed (Vy).

items.question: What action is required for Main Gear Box oil overheating above 115 °C?
options: Set IAS to Vy and monitor the CWP, landing as soon as practicable
items.explanation: Section 3.6: MGB oil overheating above 115 °C requires setting IAS to Vy and monitoring the CWP, landing as soon as practicable (or as soon as possible if temperature continues to rise).

items.question: Metal particles detected in the Tail Gear Box (TGB) oil circuit require the pilot to:
options: Avoid prolonged hovering and continue flight
Reduce power and land as soon as possible
items.explanation: Section 3.6: TGB CHIP requires avoiding prolonged hovering; the flight may be continued (this is less severe than the MGB CHIP caution, which requires reducing power and monitoring).

items.question: When the LIMIT caption illuminates in high speed cruise or a steep maneuver, what is the correct response?
options: Reduce power and reduce speed or load factor, then continue flight
items.explanation: Section 3.6 Hydraulic Alarms: LIMIT indicates the main servo unit has reached its maximum load. The pilot should reduce collective power and reduce cyclic speed/load factor, then continue flight.

items.question: If battery temperature rises above the maximum and the U bus voltage remains normal, what is the correct action?
options: BATT OFF, land as soon as practicable
GENE OFF, BATT ON, switch off unnecessary equipment, land as soon as practicable
items.explanation: Section 3.6 Electrical Alarms: for battery over-temperature with U bus above Umax, turn BATT ON, GENE OFF, switch off unnecessary equipment, and land as soon as practicable.

items.question: An AC power supply (inverter) failure, if the INV switch is confirmed ON, results in:
options: Loss of all AC consumers; continue flight with hands on the controls
items.explanation: Section 3.6: an inverter failure with INV confirmed ON causes loss of all AC consumers (the AFCS, if installed, disengages automatically); the pilot keeps hands on the controls and continues the flight.

items.question: What does a fuel quantity caution below 48 kg (106 lb) indicate?
options: Land as soon as possible; approximately 15 minutes of flight remain at MCP
Land as soon as practicable; no time constraint
The fuel gauge should be recalibrated
items.explanation: Section 3.6 Fuel Alarms: fuel quantity below 48 kg requires landing as soon as possible, with approximately 15 minutes of flight time remaining at MCP; large attitude changes should be avoided to prevent flame-out.

items.question: In case of low fuel pressure in flight, what is the correct procedure?
options: Reduce collective power and switch the fuel pump ON, landing as soon as possible
Land immediately with no other action
Increase power to clear the blockage
items.explanation: Section 3.6: low fuel pressure in flight requires reducing power, switching FUEL P/FUEL PUMP ON, and landing as soon as possible with a low-power approach, prepared for a possible flame-out.

items.question: If the fuel filter pre-clogging caution is flashing (level 1, at idle/start/shutdown), what is permitted?
options: One flight of up to 3 hours before maintenance action is required
items.explanation: Section 3.6 Fuel Alarms: a flashing fuel filter pre-clogging caption (level 1) permits one flight of up to 3 hours maximum before maintenance action is required.

items.question: If pitot heating is found inoperative, what should the pilot do?
options: Confirm PITOT is ON and monitor the airspeed indicator, continuing flight
Switch to the standby ASI only
items.explanation: Section 3.6 Miscellaneous Alarms: for pitot heating inoperative, check PITOT is ON, monitor the airspeed indicator, and continue flight.

items.question: If one or both cargo hold doors are found unlocked in flight, what is the correct action?
options: Reduce airspeed to 70 kt and land as soon as practicable
Increase airspeed to reduce door flutter
items.explanation: Section 3.6: one or both cargo hold doors unlocked requires reducing airspeed to 70 kt (130 km/h) and landing as soon as practicable, with a low rate of descent on approach.

items.question: What distinguishes a flight control hardover from a servojam?
options: A hardover causes uncommanded control movement; a servojam causes higher-than-normal force to move the controls
A hardover only affects the tail rotor; a servojam only affects the collective
A servojam only occurs on the ground
items.explanation: Section 3.7: a hardover results in uncommanded movement of one or two flight controls (including yaw); a servojam results in a higher than normal force required to move the flight controls.
